title: M0 Integration & Merge Closure
intent: Turn the cumulative Target read, native Go command, Temporal workflow, and projection compatibility work into an isolated, reproducible, reviewable merge candidate.
scope: Establish a clean test baseline, verify fresh and upgraded databases, prove one-database TypeScript-to-Go-to-Temporal delivery and recovery, close integration defects, split the cumulative working tree into reviewable commits, and record a truthful merge decision.
non_goals: Implement Graph Engine, RunWorkflow, Execution Gateway, Submission, Review, or Acceptance
Rewrite inherited TypeScript features that are unrelated to the Target vertical slice
Change Target authority or permit compatibility reads to mutate immutable snapshots
Push, merge, deploy, release, or create a ship record without separate explicit approval
acceptance_criteria: Target-focused TypeScript tests, Go tests, workspace typecheck, build, token gates, diff checks, and the repository-wide test suite pass in an isolated reproducible environment or every inherited failure is proven against the unchanged base commit and explicitly excluded from the merge delta.
A fresh PostgreSQL database and a representative pre-Target database both migrate through the current journal without schema or data loss errors.

One documented local entry point starts or connects the TypeScript compatibility edge, Go Domain API, PostgreSQL, Temporal service, and Go orchestration worker with explicit health signals and shared configuration.

On one PostgreSQL database, native Target creation commits TargetRevision, AuditEvent, and Outbox facts; the worker delivers the event to a stable TargetWorkflow; duplicate delivery is idempotent; and service or worker restart does not lose the workflow state.
Compatibility Target list, detail, immutable revision, corrupt projection isolation, bounded legacy upgrade, and operator reconciliation remain covered and usable after the unified-stack changes.
The cumulative work is organized into logical, reviewable commits with migration ordering preserved, no unrelated files included, and a clean working tree after evidence records are committed.
The final review record states ready, not ready, or needs human decision without self-approving merge or release.
